newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: OPTIONS -- CALLS ON DUTCH BANKS IN FAVOUR ON EOE.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS -- CALLS ON DUTCH BANKS IN FAVOUR ON EOE.

text.p: Call options on bank ABN AMRO and bank/insurer Internationale Nederlanden Groep (ING) dominated almost 30 percent of trading on the European Options Exchange on Monday as interest rates remained favourable.

Bank stocks are the most sensitive to changes in interest rates and benefited from higher than expected U.S. unemployment which neutralised fears for wage demands and subsequent inflation and interest rate hike jitters there, one dealer said.
But investors also bought ING calls as they hoped there was some merit in rumours it was preparing a takeover of Winterthur insurance, effectively also giving it a large stake in BBL.
Over 21,000 ING call options changed hands, compared with only 700 puts.

"This is mainly end-investors buying calls and not yet rolling over of October options -- expiring next Friday -- to November," one dealer said, adding roll-overs would only start to take place if share prices began sinking.
On the contrary, the cash market moved to its next record high, with the AEX touching 588.59 points early in the day, up from Friday's record close of 584.93.
ABN AMRO calls amounted to almost 12,000, compared with 2,200 puts, as investors looked at proceeds from MeesPierson.
ABN AMRO signed a letter of intent on Friday to sell MeesPierson to Fortis for at least two billion guilders.
Index options were also well traded as small investors were bullish on the AEX and were buying calls.
"Small investors are really keen on calls, which makes me a bit cautious. It looks too early for the suckers' rally just yet, but who knows," one trader said.
